question: Does the search-space artefact demonstrated on cysteine appear, with the same instrument, for a modification of a different residue whose near-isobaric alternative is usually absent from the search space?

pair.delta_source: computed by the analysis script from element masses in cys-audit/src/cys_audit/constants.py, not quoted in this file

instrument.extension: one table entry (phosphorylation, sulfation) plus the element masses H and P
instrument.version_policy: bump the tool version and archive the previous version byte for byte, as versions 0.1.0 and 0.2.0 were archived

dataset_selection_rule.qualifies_if: projectFileNames contain both parameters.txt and modificationSpecificPeptides.txt
dataset_selection_rule.take: the first qualifying candidate; if its two files exceed 200 MB together, the next
dataset_selection_rule.record: the full ordered candidate list goes in the audit
dataset_selection_rule.if_none: widen to pages 1 and 2 and record it; if still none, report the round as blocked on data

branches.B1: sulfation absent from the variable modifications AND at least SEARCHSPACE_FAIL_SHARE of the identified phosphopeptides at or above M* at the deposit's own main-search tolerance -> FAIL, reported as the same structural artefact outside cysteine chemistry, with the share stated
branches.B2: sulfation present among the variable modifications -> the artefact does not apply here; report it as found and audit the next qualifying candidate as well
branches.B3: tolerance or modification list unreadable from the deposit's own files -> UNDECIDABLE; the tolerance is not guessed and no share is quoted
branches.B4: fewer than 200 identified phosphopeptides with a usable mass -> underpowered; no share quoted

controls.PC1: the extended table still reproduces the cysteine delta 0.017758 Da
controls.PC2: adding sulfation to the search-space list moves the status away from FAIL
controls.PC3: at a tolerance where M* exceeds every observed peptide mass the status is not FAIL
controls.NC1: a modification outside the table returns UNDECIDABLE 'not covered', never PASS
controls.PC4: the released test suite passes after the extension, new tests included

what_this_cannot_show: that any particular identification in the deposit is wrong

anything about prior odds: sulfation on S, T and Y is far rarer than phosphorylation and is labile, so most such identifications are very probably phosphopeptides; the artefact is about what the data can decide
fragment-level discrimination or neutral-loss behaviour, which are not modelled
anything obtained by re-searching raw files, which this round does not do
